approved: Migration Agents Registration Application Charge Amendment (Rates of Charge) Bill 2019

Labor did not oppose the Migration Amendment (Regulation of Migration Agents) Bill 2019 and related charge bill, but moved a second reading amendment criticising the government for taking over five years to act on the 2014 Kendall review recommendations. The bills remove the requirement for lawyers with unrestricted practising certificates to register as migration agents, instead regulating them through state and territory professional bodies.

The speaker argued that the Migration Amendment (Regulation of Migration Agents) Bill 2019 and the Migration Agents Registration Application Charge Amendment (Rates of Charge) Bill 2019 would cut red tape by removing dual regulation for legal practitioners, saving small practices from unnecessary costs and training. The bills remove unrestricted lawyers from Migration Agents Registration Authority regulation, give restricted lawyers two years to transition, and adjust registration charges for non-commercial migration advice providers.

The speaker supported the Migration Amendment (Regulation of Migration Agents) Bill and the Migration Agents Registration Application Charge Amendment (Rates of Charge) Bill 2019, which remove dual registration requirements for lawyers providing immigration assistance and update definitions, but argued the bills are long overdue—based on 2014 recommendations and first introduced in 2017—and backed Labor’s amendments for Senate scrutiny.

The speaker argued the bills partially implement recommendation 1 of the 2014 OMARA review, removing lawyers from the migration agents regulatory scheme to allow legal practitioners to register as migration agents, and noted previous support for the legislation.
